# EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment

ZiAn Wang^(1,\*), Ruiqi Liu^(2,\*), Zhengbo Zhang^(2,\*), Yi Han³,
Jialiang Shen⁴, Ruoxin Chen⁵ Manni Cui⁶, Ximo Zhu², Jin Jiang⁷, Mingzhe
Liu⁸, Linhao Wang¹, Wenhao Wang^(9,$`\dagger`$), Shu Wu^(2,$`\dagger`$)
¹Jilin University ²Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of
Sciences ³Southwest University ⁴University of Sydney ⁵Tencent Youtu
Lab ⁶Huazhong University of Science and Technology ⁷United Arab Emirates
University ⁸Shenzhen University ⁹Vast Intelligence Lab ^(\*)Equal
contribution.  ^($`\dagger`$)Corresponding authors.

###### Abstract

Determining whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether
the situation it depicts is factually supported. We formulate Image
Factuality Assessment: given an image and a generic verification
instruction, a system returns a supported or refuted verdict with an
evidence-grounded explanation. Without a supplied textual claim, the
system must progressively refine factual questions during investigation
and align external evidence with the specific situation depicted. We
introduce EviLens, an expert-reviewed benchmark of 10,174 supported and
refuted images from controlled construction and web collection, covering
twelve factual error types and evaluating both verdict accuracy and
evidence sufficiency. We develop EviScene, a multimodal ReAct agent that
interleaves visual inspection, external retrieval, and evidence
analysis, using new findings to refine its questions and revisit
relevant image details. We train a compact policy with supervised
fine-tuning on reviewed teacher trajectories, followed by privileged
on-policy self-distillation applied to verified decisions from the
policy’s own investigations. On the 1,527-image test set, the trained
Qwen3.5-9B agent achieves 79.05% balanced accuracy and a Strict Evidence
Sufficiency Rate (SESR) of 52.26%, improving over the same-backbone base
agent by 6.71 and 9.37 percentage points, respectively. Its SESR is the
highest among the evaluated agents.

Code, models, and data will be released at
[https://github.com/wangzian828/EVISCENE](https://github.com/wangzian828/EVISCENE)
and
[https://huggingface.co/ZiAnwang/EviScene](https://huggingface.co/ZiAnwang/EviScene).

## 1 Introduction

![Refer to caption](2610.14609v1/fig1_task_comparison_claim_compact.png)

Figure 1: Claim-guided versus image-centered verification. EviScene
alternates evidence retrieval and visual reinspection to refine
questions about the depicted event and its context.

Visual fact-checking uses external evidence to assess the factual
accuracy of image content and explain the resulting judgment. Recent
work has explored automating this process by combining multimodal models
with web retrieval, image search, and evidence analysis ([Akhtar et al.,
2023](#bib.bib2); [Qi et al., 2024](#bib.bib32); [Braun et al.,
2025](#bib.bib7)). We focus on image-centered verification, asking
whether the depicted situation has factual support rather than how the
image was produced.

We refer to this task as _Image Factuality Assessment_: given a single
image and a generic verification instruction, but no supplied textual
claim, a system returns a supported or refuted verdict with an
evidence-grounded explanation. The assessment concerns the factual
situation conveyed by the image’s visible content, including the
identities, activities, relationships, and spatiotemporal context that
determine its interpretation.

This setting presents two main challenges. First, an initial visual
inspection is often insufficient to clarify and verify the complex
factual situation depicted in an image. In claim-centered benchmarks
such as AVerImaTeC, a supplied textual statement anchors evidence
retrieval ([CAO et al., 2025](#bib.bib10)). In our setting, the model
instead draws on visual content and newly obtained evidence to formulate
and refine questions about facts central to the image’s meaning. Second,
retrieved evidence must be aligned with the specific situation depicted
in the image. Material about the same person or place may concern a
different activity, year, or stage; a shared person or place alone is
insufficient to support the verdict. Addressing these challenges
requires interleaving visual inspection with evidence gathering, using
intermediate findings to refine what should be checked next.
Figure [1](#S1.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
contrasts this image-centered setting with claim-guided verification.

![Refer to caption](2610.14609v1/EviLens-taxonomy-line-polish.png)

Figure 2: Factual errors in EviLens: (a) constructed and collected
examples with corresponding evidence; (b) the twelve error types grouped
into three families.

To support research and evaluation in this setting, we introduce
EviLens, a benchmark comprising 10,174 images: 3,114 supported and 7,060
refuted. Its twelve factual error types fall into three families: event
and relation, attribute and detail, and context. We obtain images
through controlled construction and web collection. Controlled
construction specifies and checks the depicted factual content,
including designated errors in refuted examples; web collection
preserves the diversity of naturally circulating content. All examples
undergo manual screening, and their factual descriptions are retained
together with the relevant construction or provenance records.
Evaluation considers both verdict accuracy and the sufficiency of the
evidence presented in the accompanying explanation.

We further develop EviScene, a multimodal agent built on ReAct ([Yao
et al., 2022](#bib.bib42)) that integrates visual inspection, web and
image retrieval, source reading, and reference-image comparison. At each
step, the policy uses the input image and accumulated investigation
history to reason about an unresolved factual question and select the
next tool action. New observations guide question refinement and
subsequent actions, such as more targeted searches or renewed inspection
of relevant image regions. The final report cites the observations
supporting its verdict.

We train Qwen3.5-9B through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on reviewed
teacher trajectories. We then apply privileged on-policy
self-distillation (PSD; [Sleiman, 2026](#bib.bib37)) to selected
decisions from the policy’s own investigations, using verified
hint-guided continuations to supervise the policy under its original
context without exposing the hint to the student.

On the 1,527-image EviLens test set, EviScene improves evidence
sufficiency over direct judgment across all five backbones evaluated in
both settings. With Qwen3.5-9B, the full SFT+PSD policy achieves 79.05%
balanced accuracy (BAcc) and a Strict Evidence Sufficiency Rate (SESR)
of 52.26%. These scores exceed those of the base agent with the same
backbone and investigation interface by 6.71 and 9.37 percentage points,
respectively. The full policy achieves the highest SESR among all
evaluated agents on the held-out test set.

Our contributions are threefold:

1.  1.  We formulate Image Factuality Assessment and introduce EviLens, a
        benchmark comprising 10,174 supported and refuted images. It covers
        twelve factual error types and supports joint evaluation of verdict
        accuracy and evidence sufficiency.
2.  2.  We develop EviScene, a multimodal ReAct agent that interleaves
        visual analysis, external retrieval, and evidence inspection. It
        uses intermediate findings to refine factual questions and returns a
        verdict with an explanation citing the evidence used.
3.  3.  We train a compact open-weight policy for multi-step visual
        fact-checking by applying SFT and PSD to reviewed trajectories and
        verified decisions. Across multiple backbones, we evaluate
        agent-based verification and analyze training effects, tool
        contributions, and performance across image sources and generators.

## 2 Related Work

#### Visual authenticity and factual verification.

Visual authenticity research covers synthetic-content detection and
factual interpretation. One line of work focuses on determining whether
an image or video is AI-generated ([Chen et al., 2025](#bib.bib13); [Liu
et al.](#bib.bib22), [2025](#bib.bib22), [2026](#bib.bib23); [Cui
et al., 2026](#bib.bib14)). Other work evaluates whether depicted
content is consistent with factual knowledge or commonsense ([Lim
et al., 2025](#bib.bib20); [Huang et al., 2025](#bib.bib18); [Niu
et al., 2026](#bib.bib27); [Bitton-Guetta et al., 2023](#bib.bib6)).
Related work also studies factually grounded refinement and reasoning
about semantic visual anomalies in generated images ([Lim et al.,
2026](#bib.bib21); [Tan et al., 2026](#bib.bib38)). Contextual
verification examines mismatches between images and their accompanying
context and seeks to recover an image’s source, time, and location ([Luo
et al., 2021](#bib.bib24); [Aneja et al., 2023](#bib.bib3);
[Papadopoulos et al., 2024](#bib.bib31); [Tonglet et al.,
2024](#bib.bib39)). Evidence-based multimodal fact-checking verifies
supplied claims using external information ([Yao et al.,
2023](#bib.bib41); [CAO et al., 2025](#bib.bib10); [Qi et al.,
2024](#bib.bib32)). DEFAME ([Braun et al., 2025](#bib.bib7)) combines
adaptive tool selection and iterative evidence collection within a
six-stage verification pipeline. In Image Factuality Assessment, the
system receives an image and a generic verification instruction, without
a supplied textual claim. EviScene uses a single ReAct policy to refine
image-grounded questions and select each next tool action from the
accumulated interaction history, then returns an evidence-grounded
verdict. Its label reflects the factuality of the depicted situation,
regardless of how the image was produced.

#### Multimodal agents and policy learning.

ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool use to support multi-step
investigation ([Yao et al., 2022](#bib.bib42)). Multimodal search and
browsing approaches use intermediate findings to guide subsequent
retrieval and visual analysis ([Zhang et al., 2026a](#bib.bib45); [Zhang
et al., 2026b](#bib.bib46)). For policy learning, agent fine-tuning uses
interaction trajectories to supervise reasoning and tool use ([Chen
et al., 2023](#bib.bib12); [Zeng et al., 2024](#bib.bib44)).
Complementary approaches adapt training data or supervision to states
visited by the current policy through on-policy data evolution ([Huang
et al., 2026](#bib.bib17)) and distillation ([Agarwal et al.,
2024](#bib.bib1); [Sleiman, 2026](#bib.bib37)). EviScene builds on this
work for image-centered verification, using new evidence to refine
factual questions and guide the reinspection of relevant image details.
We first fine-tune the policy on reviewed teacher trajectories and then
apply privileged on-policy self-distillation to decisions reached during
its investigations.

## 3 EviLens

EviLens evaluates models’ ability to verify the factual situation
conveyed by an image and justify their verdict with external evidence.
The benchmark contains 10,174 images from controlled construction and
web collection: 3,114 supported and 7,060 refuted.

### 3.1 Twelve Factual Error Types

The taxonomy organizes factual discrepancies around three questions:
_Did the depicted event occur, or did the depicted relation hold? Is the
visible attribute or detail correct? Is the content presented in its
true context?_ The twelve error types are grouped into three
corresponding families: event and relation, attribute and detail, and
context
(Figure [2](#S1.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")(b)).
Figure [2](#S1.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")(a)
illustrates representative discrepancies by comparing visible content
with the corresponding external evidence.

![Refer to caption](2610.14609v1/EviLens-pipeline-line-polish.png)

Figure 3: Construction and collection of EviLens. The curation agent
builds and checks candidates, uses feedback to guide later rounds, and
submits them for expert review.

For each generated refuted image, we assign a primary error type to
guide construction and check whether the resulting image exhibits the
intended discrepancy. For collected refuted images, we assign error
types after acquisition to describe the factual error mechanism in each
image. Operational definitions and distinctions between neighboring
types are given in
Appendix [A.4](#A1.SS4 "A.4 Error-Type Definitions ‣ Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment").
An image may contain several visible details, but its primary type
identifies the discrepancy that decides the refuted label. This keeps
the error analysis tied to the fact being verified. The same taxonomy
also tracks factual errors across constructed and collected refuted
images. Its category describes the error, not the image’s acquisition
route, production method, or visual style.

### 3.2 Construction and Collection

The curation agent in
Figure [3](#S3.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 3.1 Twelve Factual Error Types ‣ 3 EviLens ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
plans searches based on coverage gaps, source diversity, and time
windows, then reads the retrieved sources and prepares candidate
examples. For controlled construction, the agent uses factual material
to specify the content to be rendered and checks the resulting image
against that specification. For web collection, it starts from existing
images and recovers the factual descriptions and evidence associated
with their visible content, while retaining the diversity of naturally
circulating material. Both pathways retain evidence for their supported
examples.

Generated supported images depict situations established by factual
references. For generated refuted images, counterfactual construction
alters a selected detail or relation in a documented situation, whereas
fabrication depicts an occurrence involving real entities that conflicts
with relevant records or constraints. Web collection contributes
supported images corroborated by source material and refuted images from
fact-checking sources. The collected material includes both photographs
and circulating synthetic images.

Automated checks assess visual clarity and evidence alignment and screen
for duplication and leakage. The results inform subsequent planning. Two
domain experts review each candidate image with its factual description
and retained records, checking visual clarity, the grounding of the
verification target, and the evidence supporting its interpretation and
label. For constructed refuted images, they also confirm that the
intended discrepancy is visible. A third domain expert resolves
disagreements. Review outcomes are acceptance, acceptance with edits, or
rejection.

Each retained example includes an image, its factual label and
explanation, relevant evidence, and the associated construction or
provenance records. The dataset is divided into 8,647 training images
and 1,527 test images. Related images from the same source or event are
grouped when constructing the splits. At evaluation, the task input
consists only of the image and a generic verification instruction. We
use private reference material to check the verdict and the grounds
stated in each response.
Appendix [A](#A1 "Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
details the five acquisition pathways, screening criteria, dataset
composition, and split construction, including source-wise label counts.

![Refer to caption](2610.14609v1/EviScene-agent-line-polish.png)

Figure 4: EviScene investigation and reporting. (a) Three tool groups
available at every investigation turn. (b) An illustrative ReAct
sequence: observations guide question refinement and tool selection,
while each interaction is appended to the history. (c) At reporting turn
$`T`$, the policy uses the input image and full history of turns
$`1,\ldots,T-1`$ to generate a verdict, explanation, and cited
observations.

## 4 EviScene

EviScene combines an image-centered investigation agent with two-stage
policy training. The agent interleaves visual inspection with external
evidence gathering within a shared ReAct history ([Yao et al.,
2022](#bib.bib42)). We train its policy through full-trajectory
supervised fine-tuning followed by PSD on selected decisions from its
own investigations.
Figure [4](#S3.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 3.2 Construction and Collection ‣ 3 EviLens ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
illustrates the investigation process;
Appendix [B](#A2 "Appendix B Implementation and Training Details ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
gives the tool and training details.

### 4.1 Image-Centered Multimodal Investigation

Given an input image $`x`$, we write the investigation history before
turn $`t`$ as

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |

       ``` math
       H_{t}=(r_{1},a_{1},o_{1},\ldots,r_{t-1},a_{t-1},o_{t-1}),
       ```                                                        |     |

where $`r_{i}`$ is the policy’s reasoning, $`a_{i}`$ its tool action,
and $`o_{i}`$ the raw observation.

At each investigation turn $`t`$, the policy $`\pi_{\theta}`$ produces a
short reasoning step and one native tool action:

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
(r_{t},a_{t})\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x,H_{t}),\qquad o_{t}=\mathcal{T}_{a_{t}}(x,H_{t}),
``` |  |

where $`\mathcal{T}_{a_{t}}`$ denotes the execution of tool action
$`a_{t}`$, which returns observation $`o_{t}`$. We append the resulting
tuple $`(r_{t},a_{t},o_{t})`$ to $`H_{t}`$ to obtain $`H_{t+1}`$. This
process repeats until the policy completes the investigation or exhausts
its action budget.

EviScene provides three tool groups. Visual tools inspect scenes and
selected regions, read and localize text, count objects, examine
relations, and perform evidence-guided visual reinspection. Retrieval
tools support web search, text-based image search, and reverse-image
search. Evidence tools inspect source pages and compare the input image
with retrieved reference images.

Retrieved material about the same person or place may concern a
different event, time, or stage. The policy therefore reads source pages
or compares retrieved images with the input to determine whether the
information supports or contradicts the fact being checked. The policy
uses each observation to refine the current factual question and guide
its next action. For example, an external identification can prompt it
to reinspect the relevant image region, text, or relation.

Let $`T`$ denote the final reporting turn, so that $`H_{T}`$ contains
all preceding tool interactions. The policy generates the final report
from the input image and this history:

|     |                                          |     |
|-----|------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       (\hat{y},\hat{e},C)=J_{\theta}(x,H_{T}),
       ```                                       |     |

where $`\hat{y}\in\{\mathrm{supported},\mathrm{refuted}\}`$ is the
factual verdict, $`\hat{e}`$ is the explanation, and $`C`$ contains the
observations from $`H_{T}`$ cited in the explanation as substantive
evidence for the verdict.

### 4.2 Full-Trajectory Supervised Fine-Tuning

We use Qwen3.5-397B-A17B ([Qwen Team, 2026](#bib.bib33)) to generate
teacher trajectories through the same agent interface used at inference.
Each trajectory records the model-visible reasoning, tool calls,
observations, retrieved images, and final report. We retain a trajectory
only if it is structurally complete and its recorded observations
support the final report.

We perform full-parameter SFT on Qwen3.5-9B ([Qwen Team,
2026](#bib.bib33)) using 4,872 reviewed teacher trajectories. Training
runs for three epochs with a learning rate of $`10^{-5}`$. Each training
trajectory retains the context for every action and the final report.
For a trajectory token sequence $`z_{1:n}`$, we minimize the weighted
loss

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SFT}}=-\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_{i}\log p_{\theta}(z_{i}\mid z_{<i}),
``` |  |

where $`w_{i}=2`$ for tool-call and final-report tokens, $`w_{i}=1`$ for
reasoning tokens, and $`w_{i}=0`$ for instruction and tool-observation
tokens. Instruction and tool-observation tokens remain in the context
but do not contribute to the loss; associated images are also retained
as conditioning inputs. This weighting emphasizes tool calls and the
final report while retaining supervision on reasoning.

|    Method |    BAcc |    Macro F1 |    Supported recall |    Refuted recall |    SESR |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| Direct visual judgment |  |  |  |  |  |

|  GPT-5.2 |  65.84 |  55.41 |  85.94 |  45.74 |  2.95 |

### 4.3 Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation

After SFT, we apply privileged on-policy self-distillation (PSD;
[Sleiman, 2026](#bib.bib37)) to selected decisions in the policy’s own
investigations.

#### Decision localization and continuation verification.

We use Gemini 3.7 Flash ([Google DeepMind, 2026a](#bib.bib15)) as a
training-only intervention model to localize decisions, construct hints,
and review continuations. At the start of each PSD round, we freeze a
copy of the current policy as $`\pi_{\bar{\theta}}`$ and collect new
investigation trajectories. From these trajectories, the localizer
selects a student decision at turn $`t`$ involving search direction,
event association, visual evidence, or the interpretation of retrieved
evidence. It is instructed to identify the earliest recoverable error
and support its selection with the original step index and recorded
observations, rather than relying solely on an incorrect final verdict.

The hint constructor may consult training-only information to propose a
short procedural hint $`h_{t}`$. At the selected decision, the hint
provides procedural guidance without revealing the answer, specifying an
exact tool action or query, or supplying a case-specific solution. We
insert $`h_{t}`$ into the original context $`c_{t}`$ at the selected
decision to form the teacher context $`\tilde{c}_{t}`$:

|     |                                                   |     |
|-----|---------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \tilde{c}_{t}=\operatorname{insert}(c_{t},h_{t}).
       ```                                                |     |

The frozen Qwen policy $`\pi_{\bar{\theta}}`$ continues the
investigation from $`\tilde{c}_{t}`$ until it generates the final
report. We accept the continuation for training only if the selected
decision is corrected, the final report is correct and
evidence-supported, and the trajectory passes the audit. The complete
continuation is used for verification, whereas distillation uses the
frozen policy’s token-level probability distributions only for the
selected assistant completion.

#### Privileged self-distillation.

The student is trained to match the frozen teacher’s top-$`K`$ token
probabilities at each position in the selected assistant completion. We
also extract preservation targets from successful investigations to
retain behavior supported by complete investigations.

Let $`\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{PSD}}`$ denote the set of accepted repair and
preservation targets. For each target
$`d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{PSD}}`$, $`u_{d}`$ denotes the token sequence
of the selected assistant completion, and $`c_{d}^{T}`$ and
$`c_{d}^{S}`$ denote the teacher and student contexts. For a repair
target associated with turn $`t`$, $`c_{d}^{T}=\tilde{c}_{t}`$ and
$`c_{d}^{S}=c_{t}`$; for a preservation target, $`c_{d}^{T}=c_{d}^{S}`$.
Each target retains the recorded image and tool context.

At each position $`\ell`$ in $`u_{d}`$, the frozen teacher distribution
is conditioned on $`c_{d}^{T}`$ and the completion prefix
$`u_{d,<\ell}`$. We retain its top-$`K`$ tokens $`\mathcal{K}_{d,\ell}`$
and renormalize their probabilities to obtain $`\bar{q}_{d,\ell}`$. We
minimize the distillation loss

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{PSD}}=-\sum_{d\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{PSD}}}\sum_{\ell=1}^{|u_{d}|}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{K}_{d,\ell}}\bar{q}_{d,\ell}(v)\log p_{\theta}\!\left(v\mid c_{d}^{S},u_{d,<\ell}\right).
``` |  |

Both target types receive the same per-target weight, and the loss is
summed over the supervised token positions in each selected completion.
The updated policy then generates new investigation trajectories for the
next round.

## 5 Experiments

### 5.1 Experimental Setup and Evaluation Protocol

#### Test set.

The EviLens test set contains 1,527 images: 377 supported and 1,150
refuted.

#### Compared systems.

We compare direct judgment and EviScene on five shared backbones:
GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, and
Qwen3.5-9B. Additional direct-judgment baselines include GPT-5.2, Claude
Opus 4.8, Kimi K2.6, Doubao Seed 2.0 Pro, MiniMax-M3, and GLM-4.6V
(Table [1](#S4.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Full-Trajectory Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ 4 EviScene ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")).
For Qwen3.5-9B, we evaluate direct judgment (Direct), the base agent
(Base), the SFT policy (SFT), and the SFT+PSD policy (Full). All agents
share a runtime with a maximum of 24 actions per investigation. Web and
text-based image search use Serper, and reverse-image search uses Serper
Lens. Jina Reader retrieves webpage content, while the Baidu general OCR
API transcribes and localizes visible text. Fact-checking websites are
blocked from evidence access during investigation. Model-mediated visual
inspection and page-evidence extraction use separate requests to the
agent’s own backbone. For Qwen3.5-9B, these requests use the checkpoint
corresponding to the evaluated configuration: Base, SFT, or Full.
Appendix [B](#A2 "Appendix B Implementation and Training Details ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
gives the model sources and tool configurations. For each shared
backbone, Direct answers from the image, while EviScene can inspect tool
observations before its final judgment. The additional direct baselines
provide reference points for the same image-level task. Both settings
use the same held-out test images and final-response criteria.

#### Metrics.

We report balanced accuracy (BAcc), macro F1, and class-wise recall.
BAcc averages supported and refuted recall. Strict Evidence Sufficiency
Rate (SESR) is the percentage of cases with a correct verdict and
sufficient grounds for the decisive image-grounded fact.

#### Evaluation protocol.

We use Gemini 3.7 Flash ([Google DeepMind, 2026a](#bib.bib15)) to assess
each final response against private reference material. The shared
criteria cover verdict correctness, factual alignment, and the
sufficiency of the grounds stated in the response.
Appendix [C](#A3 "Appendix C Evaluation Protocol ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
provides the full metric definitions and evaluation criteria.

### 5.2 Main Results

#### Investigation improves evidence sufficiency across backbones.

Across the five shared backbones in
Table [1](#S4.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Full-Trajectory Supervised Fine-Tuning ‣ 4 EviScene ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment"),
EviScene improves SESR over direct judgment by 27.11 to 46.82 percentage
points. BAcc also improves for four of the five backbones. For
Qwen3.5-9B, the Base agent raises BAcc from 65.70% to 72.34% and SESR
from 1.70% to 42.89%, without SFT or PSD. Some direct models show
pronounced verdict preferences: Gemini 3.1 Pro recalls 96.52% of refuted
but only 28.65% of supported cases, while GLM-4.6V has 95.49% supported
and 24.43% refuted recall. The exception to the BAcc trend is Gemini 3.1
Pro: its BAcc changes from 62.58% to 62.42% with investigation, even as
SESR rises from 5.57% to 32.68%. For the other three paired backbones,
investigation changes BAcc by 2.26 points for GPT-5.5, 5.93 for
Gemini 3.7 Flash, and 3.04 for Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Their SESR gains are
46.82, 33.79, and 36.61 points, respectively. Gemini 3.7 Flash gains
12.73 points in supported recall and loses 0.87 in refuted recall;
Qwen3.5-397B-A17B loses 5.57 and gains 11.65 points, respectively.

| Variant                 | BAcc  | SESR  |
|-------------------------|-------|-------|
| All tools (Full)        | 79.05 | 52.26 |
| w/o web search          | 74.37 | 35.89 |
| w/o image retrieval     | 74.52 | 40.01 |
| w/o evidence inspection | 76.55 | 46.04 |

Table 3: Tool-family ablations (%).

#### The full compact policy leads in SESR.

The full Qwen3.5-9B policy achieves the highest SESR (52.26%) and
second-highest BAcc (79.05%) among the evaluated agents. It also
outperforms the substantially larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B agent by 7.33
percentage points in BAcc and 8.97 percentage points in SESR under the
same action limit.

### 5.3 Training and Tool Analysis

#### Training-stage analysis.

For Qwen3.5-9B, Base recalls 93.48% of refuted cases but only 51.19% of
supported cases. SFT raises supported recall to 76.39% while refuted
recall falls to 81.22%, moving BAcc from 72.34% to 78.81% and SESR from
42.89% to 50.49%. SFT narrows the gap between supported and refuted
recall from 42.29 to 4.83 percentage points. After PSD, supported recall
rises to 80.11% and refuted recall falls to 78.00%; their gap narrows
from 4.83 to 2.11 percentage points. Relative to SFT, Full gains 0.24
points in BAcc and 1.77 points in SESR. Macro F1 is 75.69% for SFT and
74.67% for Full. Overall, Full exceeds Base by 6.71 BAcc points and 9.37
SESR points.

#### Tool ablations.

We disable one external-evidence tool family at a time from the full
Qwen3.5-9B policy
(Table [3](#S5.T3 "Table 3 ‣ Investigation improves evidence sufficiency across backbones. ‣ 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")),
retaining direct visual operations. All variants use the same prompt,
action budget, judgment procedure, and test set.

Relative to Full, removing web search lowers BAcc/SESR by 4.68/16.37
points; image retrieval by 4.53/12.25; and evidence inspection by
2.50/6.22. SESR falls more in every case.
Appendix [B.2](#A2.SS2 "B.2 Agent Runtime and Tools ‣ Appendix B Implementation and Training Details ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
lists the exact operations disabled for each tool family.

### 5.4 Source and Generator Analysis

#### Acquisition sources.

Table [2](#S5.T2 "Table 2 ‣ Evaluation protocol. ‣ 5.1 Experimental Setup and Evaluation Protocol ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
reports results by image source and generator. From Direct to Full, SESR
rises from 1.29% to 52.75% on constructed images and from 3.46% to
50.17% on web-collected images. Relative to Base, Full improves SESR by
8.81 and 11.76 percentage points on the two sources, respectively. Full
also achieves similar BAcc on both, at 76.75% and 77.21%.

#### Image generators.

Full improves both BAcc and SESR over Base on images from all three
generators. It achieves 46.98% SESR on Nano Banana Pro, 58.39% on GPT
Image 2, and 54.64% on Seedream 5.0 Lite. GPT Image 2 and Seedream 5.0
Lite are not used to construct training images, so the gains over Base
are not limited to the training generator.

### 5.5 Qualitative Analysis

Figure [5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ Privileged self-distillation. ‣ 4.3 Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation ‣ 4 EviScene ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
illustrates four comparisons. The display and Plan Cabaret cases require
records of the named certification tier and launch event; the Cassini
poster requires the exhibition schedule. For the museum, the evidence
must distinguish an opening from the documented construction stage. Each
case ties the checked evidence to the depicted text, subject, or
activity.

## 6 Discussion and Conclusion

We formulated Image Factuality Assessment, in which a system verifies
the situation depicted in an image without a supplied textual claim. We
introduced EviLens to evaluate both verdict accuracy and evidence
sufficiency. The benchmark combines controlled construction with web
collection to cover designed and circulating images. We developed
EviScene to refine factual questions through visual inspection and
external evidence gathering. We trained a compact policy using
full-trajectory SFT followed by PSD on verified decisions from its own
investigations.

Across five shared backbones, EviScene improves evidence sufficiency
over direct judgment. The trained Qwen3.5-9B policy achieves 79.05%
balanced accuracy and 52.26% SESR, the highest SESR among the evaluated
agents. Removing web search, image retrieval, or evidence inspection
reduces both metrics. These findings support verifying image content
through evidence about the depicted situation, rather than judging
factuality from visual plausibility or image origin.

### AI use statement

Generative AI tools were used to create synthetic images for the
controlled construction branches of EviLens. Each generated example
followed a predefined factual situation or factual-error type grounded
in the associated construction record. The authors manually reviewed the
generated candidates for visual clarity and consistency with the
intended factual content, and take responsibility for the final dataset
and all results reported in this paper. We also used generative AI tools
to polish the manuscript’s language. All such revisions were reviewed
and finalized by the authors.

## Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation

This appendix details the construction, factual annotation, error types,
expert review, and composition of EviLens.

### A.1 Relation to Existing Benchmarks

Table [4](#A1.T4 "Table 4 ‣ A.1 Relation to Existing Benchmarks ‣ Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
locates EviLens among adjacent resources for generated-image detection,
out-of-context detection, and multimodal fact-checking. “No claim” means
that no claim, caption, post, or generation prompt is supplied; “World
fact” requires a verdict about the depicted situation rather than
provenance, plausibility, or pairwise matching. “Evidence output”
requires evidence-bearing justification, not a label or free-form
rationale alone. Origin-independent factuality means that image origin
alone does not determine the factual label or score.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
|  Benchmark |  No claim |  World fact |  Web evidence |  Evidence output |  Origin-independent factuality |  Size |
| Generated-image detection and visual reasoning |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  GenImage \[[2023](#bib.bib48)\] |  ✓ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  2.68M images |
|  WHOOPS! \[[2023](#bib.bib6)\] |  ✓ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  500 images |
|  T2I-FactualBench \[[2025](#bib.bib18)\] |  ✗ |  ✓ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✓ |  3K prompts |
| Image-text and out-of-context verification |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  NewsCLIPpings \[[2021](#bib.bib24)\] |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  988,283 pairs |
|  COSMOS \[[2023](#bib.bib3)\] |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  204,458 images |
|  VERITE \[[2024](#bib.bib31)\] |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✗ |  ✓ |  1K pairs |
| Multimodal fact-checking |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  MOCHEG \[[2023](#bib.bib41)\] |  ✗ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✗ |  15,601 claims |
|  FACTIFY3M \[[2023](#bib.bib11)\] |  ✗ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  3M samples |
|  AVerImaTeC \[[2025](#bib.bib10)\] |  ✗ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✗ |  1,297 claims |
|  VeriTaS \[[2026](#bib.bib35)\] |  ✗ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  25K claims |
|  RW-Post \[[2026](#bib.bib40)\] |  ✗ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✗ |  1.52K + 218 cases |
|  EviLens (ours) |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  ✓ |  10,174 images |

Table 4: Comparison with representative benchmarks.

EviLens combines image-based verification without a supplied textual
claim, external reference evidence, and origin-independent factual
labels. Generated images may be supported or refuted according to the
factual content they depict. Evaluation considers both verdict accuracy
and the sufficiency of the evidence stated in the explanation.

### A.2 Construction and Collection

The curation process combines controlled construction and web
collection, as shown in
Figure [3](#S3.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 3.1 Twelve Factual Error Types ‣ 3 EviLens ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment").
For controlled construction, the agent first establishes a factual
situation from reference material and specifies the content to render.
Supported images express that situation; refuted images introduce a
selected factual error. For web collection, the agent acquires an image,
recovers the source information needed to interpret it, and assigns its
factual label and, where applicable, error type.
Table [5](#A1.T5 "Table 5 ‣ A.2 Construction and Collection ‣ Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
summarizes the five acquisition pathways.

|  Pathway |  Label |  Cases |  Factual basis |
|----|----|----|----|
|  Synthesis from factual references |  Supported |  2,073 |  Reference material establishes the situation that the generated image is intended to depict. |
|  Supported web images |  Supported |  1,041 |  Source information corroborates the depicted situation. |
|  Counterfactual construction |  Refuted |  3,106 |  A documented situation is modified through a selected visible detail or relation. |
|  Fabrication from real entities |  Refuted |  3,067 |  A constructed occurrence or relation conflicts with records or constraints applying to the depicted subjects. |
|  Images from fact-checking sources |  Refuted |  887 |  A circulating image is paired with source material explaining its factual error. |
| Total |  |  10,174 |  3,114 supported and 7,060 refuted images. |

Table 5: Acquisition pathways, retained examples, and the basis for
their factual interpretation.

In counterfactual construction, the source situation supplies the
context in which a chosen detail or relation is changed. Fabrication
instead composes an occurrence involving recognizable entities and
checks it against the relevant records or constraints. Both pathways use
the taxonomy to guide construction and then inspect the resulting image
for the intended discrepancy. Collected cases retain the factual
discrepancy documented by their source material. Collection includes
both photographs and synthetic images that have circulated online.

### A.3 Factual Annotation and Evidence

The annotation connects the image to the factual situation that
determines its interpretation. It describes the relevant subjects,
activity or relation, and context, together with the evidence supporting
or refuting that situation. Construction records preserve the intended
factual content and any selected change. Collection records preserve the
source information used to identify and interpret the visual material.
They also provide private evaluation references.

For generated supported images, review concerns the identities,
activities, relationships, and contextual details expressed in the
completed image. Reference material establishes the factual basis, and
the rendered content is checked against it. For refuted images, the
explanation identifies the depicted relation that conflicts with the
associated evidence. Visual references assess appearance and
composition, while factual interpretation follows the associated
evidence.

### A.4 Error-Type Definitions

Table [6](#A1.T6 "Table 6 ‣ A.4 Error-Type Definitions ‣ Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
expands the twelve types shown in
Figure [2](#S1.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment").
For taxonomy-driven controlled construction, each refuted image is
assigned the type that specifies its intended factual discrepancy.
Collected cases use the factual error documented by their source records
as the annotation.

|  Error type |  Definition |
|----|----|
| Event and relation errors |  |
|  Invented action |  A real subject performs an action or participates in an event that did not occur. |
|  Invented interaction |  Real subjects are depicted meeting, collaborating, or participating together when that interaction did not occur. |
|  Impossible state |  The depicted state contradicts physics, science, technology, or commonsense. |
|  False official record |  A visible roster, certificate, scoreboard, directory, or similar display presents an incorrect official role, result, ranking, or entry. |
| Attribute and detail errors |  |
|  Numerical alteration |  A visible number, count, score, measurement, or statistic has an incorrect value. |
|  Identity substitution |  The depicted person, institution, product, affiliation, or role is misidentified. |
|  Spatial alteration |  An object’s placement, orientation, relative position, or local relation is wrong. |
|  Text or mark alteration |  Visible wording, a logo, flag, formula, or short label contains incorrect content. |
| Contextual errors |  |
|  Temporal displacement |  Visible content places a subject or event at the wrong date, year, era, or time. |
|  Event recontextualization |  An identifiable scene or event is presented as a different occurrence through the image or its visible presentation. |
|  Source impersonation |  A visible post, page, account, publisher, verification marker, or platform identity is falsely attributed. |
|  Geographic displacement |  The stated venue, landmark, city, country, or region is wrong. |

Table 6: Definitions of the twelve factual error types in EviLens.

The primary discrepancy also resolves overlap between neighboring types.
Identity substitution concerns who or what occupies a role; false
official record concerns the association or result asserted by a record.
A changed number is a numerical alteration when its value is the central
error, while an incorrect official outcome is assigned to false official
record. Spatial alteration concerns local arrangement, and geographic
displacement concerns the location associated with the scene. Temporal
displacement changes the time; event recontextualization changes the
represented occurrence.

### A.5 Expert Review

Expert review follows automated construction and collection. Two domain
experts review each image together with its factual description and
retained records. They check the clarity of decisive visual details and
text, verify that the target is grounded in visible content, and assess
whether the evidence supports the required identities and context and
justifies the assigned label. For generated cases, they also check that
the intended fact or discrepancy appears in the image; for refuted
cases, they confirm the primary error type. A third expert resolves
disagreements.

Review decisions are acceptance, acceptance with edits, or rejection.
Edits address factual wording, source association, and category
assignment. Unclear or unresolved cases are rejected.

### A.6 Composition, Splits, and Availability

The dataset has 10,174 images across five pathways
(Table [5](#A1.T5 "Table 5 ‣ A.2 Construction and Collection ‣ Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")),
with 8,647 in training and 1,527 in the test set.
Table [7](#A1.T7 "Table 7 ‣ A.6 Composition, Splits, and Availability ‣ Appendix A EviLens Construction and Annotation ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
gives the source and factual-label counts for both partitions. All
retained images underwent expert review; admitted investigation
trajectories are reported in
Appendix [B.3](#A2.SS3 "B.3 SFT Data and Supervision ‣ Appendix B Implementation and Training Details ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment").

The controlled test subset contains 513 Nano Banana Pro \[[Raisinghani,
2025](#bib.bib34)\], 423 GPT Image 2 \[[OpenAI, 2026b](#bib.bib30)\],
and 302 Seedream 5.0 Lite \[[ByteDance Seed, 2026b](#bib.bib9)\] images.
Controlled training images use Nano Banana Pro; web-collected images
retain their original sources.

Related images from the same source or event are grouped when
constructing the partitions, and the test set is used for evaluation.
Systems receive only the image and generic verification instruction; the
associated annotations support assessment. Upon acceptance, we will
open-source all artifacts from this work: the complete dataset,
including images, labels, explanations, evidence and provenance records,
and fixed partitions; all data-construction, training, and evaluation
code; prompts and training trajectories; and all trained model
checkpoints.

|                         |           |         |           |         |        |
|-------------------------|-----------|---------|-----------|---------|--------|
|                         | Training  |         | Test      |         | Total  |
| Source                  | Supported | Refuted | Supported | Refuted |        |

| Web collection          | 897       | 742     | 144       | 145     | 1,928  |

### B.2 Agent Runtime and Tools

Each investigation turn produces one native tool call. The runtime
validates its arguments and remaining budget, executes it, and appends
the raw result and any associated images to the history. The policy uses
that history in the next turn. Web search uses the Serper API \[[Serper,
2026](#bib.bib36)\]. Fact-checking websites are blocked from the agent’s
evidence access, including their exclusion from web-search queries. Page
inspection uses Jina Reader \[[Jina AI, 2026](#bib.bib19)\] to fetch
webpage content, followed by model-based extraction of passages relevant
to the active question. For Qwen3.5-9B, the investigation policy and
model-mediated tools use the same checkpoint within each configuration:
Base, SFT, or Full. Model-mediated visual inspection and page-evidence
extraction are executed through separate requests. Positioned text is
obtained through the Baidu general OCR API \[[Baidu AI Cloud,
2026](#bib.bib5)\]. Search and image retrieval return candidates; page
reading or image comparison checks them before citation.

|  Operation |  Role and returned information |  Limit |
|----|----|----|
|  perceive_scene |  Scene description, entities, attributes, relations, and visible uncertainties. |  Global |
|  ocr_with_position |  Text transcription with positions for later cropping and inspection. |  3 |
|  crop_and_inspect |  Deterministic crop and focused description of a selected region. |  4 |
|  focused_visual_inspection |  Original image and derived views assessed against one evidence-motivated visual question. |  2 |
|  analyze_visual_anomalies |  Locatable physical, logical, relation, or text observations relevant to the current target. |  3 |
|  check_consistency |  Lighting, geometry, scale, boundary, and physical-relation checks for a specified aspect. |  3 |
|  count_objects |  Count and localization of a requested object type. |  Global |
|  text_search |  Ranked web results for a concrete factual query. |  16 |
|  reverse_image_search |  Visually related images and their source pages from the image or a crop. |  2 |
|  text_image_search |  Candidate reference images and associated pages from a textual query. |  6 |
|  visit |  Relevant passages and source metadata from one to three selected URLs. |  16 |
|  compare_with_reference |  Same-subject or same-event relation and concrete differences between the input and a selected reference. |  6 |
|  current_time |  Current date and time when temporal interpretation requires it. |  1 |

Table 10: Native operations available to the investigation policy.
Numeric limits are per case and remain subject to the 24-action global
budget. “Global” means that only the global budget applies.

#### Ablation configuration.

Each tool ablation disables one of the three tool families listed below,
while all remaining tools stay available. Full uses the complete tool
set. All variants use the Full policy checkpoint and share the prompt,
action budget, and terminal-judgment procedure.

|  Variant                  |  Disabled native operations               |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
|  Full                     |  None                                     |
|  w/o web search           |  text_search                              |
|  w/o image retrieval      |  text_image_search, reverse_image_search  |
|  w/o evidence inspection  |  visit, compare_with_reference            |

Table 11: Native-operation settings for the tool ablations in
Table [3](#S5.T3 "Table 3 ‣ Investigation improves evidence sufficiency across backbones. ‣ 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment").

The policy may finish before the limit through finish_investigation.
Completion or exhaustion of the action budget passes the retained
interaction to terminal judgment. This stage receives the original image
and accumulated observations, then produces the verdict and report.
Citations identify successful observations used in the explanation.
Empty results and failed requests remain in the history with their
original status.

Web and text-to-image search use the Serper web and image endpoints.
Image search returns at most three candidate image and page pairs.
Reverse-image retrieval uses Serper Lens; its semantic branch generates
one visual query and submits it to image search. Page inspection fetches
one to three selected URLs and extracts passages for the current image
fact and retrieval goal. Visual tools receive the original image or a
deterministic crop and return structured observations.

### B.3 SFT Data and Supervision

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B \[[Qwen Team, 2026](#bib.bib33)\] generates the
teacher investigations through the same tool interface used at inference
time. Each retained example includes the complete action and observation
sequence, the images available at successive turns, and a terminal
report supported by the recorded investigation. For each training image,
the teacher agent performs up to three rollout attempts. Once a complete
trajectory passes review, it is retained and no further attempt is made
for that image. We perform full-parameter fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-9B
\[[Qwen Team, 2026](#bib.bib33)\] on the 4,872 reviewed investigations.
The weighted supervision emphasizes native tool calls and the terminal
report while retaining the reasoning that led to them.

### B.4 PSD Procedure

Table [12](#A2.T12 "Table 12 ‣ B.4 PSD Procedure ‣ Appendix B Implementation and Training Details ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
follows one PSD round from fresh investigations to accepted training
targets and the policy update. Gemini 3.7 Flash \[[Google DeepMind,
2026a](#bib.bib15)\] proposes and reviews the intervention; the frozen
Qwen policy supplies the continuation and token distribution.

|  |  |
|----|----|
| 1 |  Freeze the current policy as $`\pi_{\bar{\theta}}`$ and collect fresh investigations. |
| 2 |  Select a decision $`t`$ in an eligible student investigation. |
| 3 |  Construct a procedural hint $`h_{t}`$ for that decision. |
| 4 |  Continue $`\pi_{\bar{\theta}}`$ from $`\operatorname{insert}(c_{t},h_{t})`$ through terminal judgment. |
| 5 |  Review the selected decision, completed investigation, evidence use, and trajectory structure. |
| 6 |  Add an accepted completion $`u_{d}`$ with teacher context $`c_{d}^{\mathrm{T}}=\operatorname{insert}(c_{t},h_{t})`$ and student context $`c_{d}^{\mathrm{S}}=c_{t}`$ to $`\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{rep}}`$. |
| 7 |  Extract preservation decisions from successful investigations with $`c_{d}^{\mathrm{T}}=c_{d}^{\mathrm{S}}`$ into $`\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{pres}}`$. |
| 8 |  Store the frozen policy’s top-$`K`$ probabilities for each supervised completion token. |
| 9 |  Update $`\pi_{\theta}`$ on $`\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{rep}}\cup\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{pres}}`$ using $`\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{PSD}}`$. |
| 10 |  Use the updated policy to begin the next rollout round. |

Table 12: One PSD round. Symbols follow the formulation in the main
text.

For each target, the teacher and student receive the same recorded image
inputs. Repair targets pair a hint-augmented teacher context with the
original student context. The distillation loss covers the selected
assistant completion, using renormalized top-$`K`$ probabilities from
the frozen teacher. Successful investigations supply preservation
targets with identical teacher and student contexts. Repair and
preservation targets use the same row weight.

For target $`d`$ and completion position $`\ell`$, the frozen teacher
defines

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
q_{d,\ell}(v)=p_{\bar{\theta}}\!\left(v\mid c_{d}^{\mathrm{T}},u_{d,<\ell}\right),\qquad\mathcal{K}_{d,\ell}=\operatorname{TopK}_{v}\,q_{d,\ell}(v),
``` |  |

and the retained probabilities are renormalized as

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bar{q}_{d,\ell}(v)=\frac{q_{d,\ell}(v)}{\sum_{v^{\prime}\in\mathcal{K}_{d,\ell}}q_{d,\ell}(v^{\prime})},\qquad v\in\mathcal{K}_{d,\ell}.
``` |  |

## Appendix C Evaluation Protocol

### C.1 Inputs and Evaluation Settings

Table [13](#A3.T13 "Table 13 ‣ C.1 Inputs and Evaluation Settings ‣ Appendix C Evaluation Protocol ‣ EviScene: Beyond “Is It AI?” for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment")
collects the common test input, evaluator, and execution settings. The
test images are separate from teacher trajectories and SFT or PSD
training data.

|  Setting |  Value |
|----|----|
|  Test images |  1,527: 377 supported and 1,150 refuted |
|  Evaluator |  Gemini 3.7 Flash (gemini-3.7-flash) \[[Google DeepMind, 2026a](#bib.bib15)\] |
|  Classification statistics |  BAcc, macro F1, and class recalls |
|  Evidence evaluation |  Stated grounds checked against private reference material |
|  Evaluation population |  All 1,527 test images |
|  Execution attempts |  Up to three per case; stop at the first binary verdict |

Table 13: Test set and evidence evaluation settings.

### C.2 Metrics

For each class $`c\in\mathcal{C}=\{\mathrm{s},\mathrm{r}\}`$, let
$`TP_{c}`$, $`FP_{c}`$, and $`FN_{c}`$ denote true positives, false
positives, and false negatives. The class supports are
$`n_{\mathrm{s}}=377`$ and $`n_{\mathrm{r}}=1150`$. We compute recall
and F1 as

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
R_{c}=\frac{TP_{c}}{n_{c}},\qquad F1_{c}=\frac{2TP_{c}}{2TP_{c}+FP_{c}+FN_{c}}.
``` |  | (1) |

Both classes receive equal weight in BAcc and macro F1:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathrm{BAcc}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{c\in\mathcal{C}}R_{c},\qquad\mathrm{MacroF1}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{c\in\mathcal{C}}F1_{c}.
``` |  | (2) |

Let $`e_{i}=1`$ when the verdict is correct and the response itself
provides sufficient grounds for the decisive image-grounded fact;
otherwise, $`e_{i}=0`$. We compute SESR over all 1,527 images as

|     |                                                     |     |     |
|-----|-----------------------------------------------------|-----|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \mathrm{SESR}=\frac{1}{1527}\sum_{i=1}^{1527}e_{i}.
       ```                                                  |     | (3) |

All metrics are reported as percentages.

#### Execution attempts.

Each case permits up to three attempts, stopping at the first response
with the required binary verdict. Cases with content-based refusals in
all three attempts are counted as incorrect predictions for their
ground-truth class.

### C.3 Assessment of Complete Responses

The evaluator checks verdict correctness, factual alignment, and
evidence sufficiency against private reference material. The grounds
stated in the response must establish the decisive image-grounded fact
or another image-grounded sub-fact that logically establishes the same
verdict. Equivalent wording, alternative evidence sources, and different
investigation paths are accepted when these criteria are met. A response
receives SESR credit when all three criteria are satisfied.

separates the recalls of supported and refuted images to show how their
contributions vary across systems.

#### Accuracy and evidence sufficiency.

Investigation consistently moves systems upward along the SESR axis,
while its effect on BAcc varies across backbones. Training moves the
compact Qwen policy toward the upper-right region with stronger verdict
accuracy and greater evidence sufficiency.

#### Recall across factual labels.

Several direct models lie far from the equal-recall guide. For the
Qwen3.5-9B agent, SFT raises supported recall and lowers refuted recall,
closing their gap.
